result.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
result.summary: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $π_v/β_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(π_v/β_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究网络上互相观察的多个 agent 各自以 KL 正则化偏好步对齐模型时，集体策略实际实现哪种聚合规则，并刻画参考项或挑战项被聚合时分别得到基数规则、序数规则（maximal lottery）或无法确定权重的情形，权重由长期注意力份额与温度决定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按注意力权重与温度聚合多个 KL 正则化策略、区分基数与序数聚合」可能为 LVR 中汇总多条 latent 推理路径或多种视觉证据假设提供概念框架，可供核查何时加权平均即可、何时只能用投票式（maximal lottery）式聚合。
